drills.q: Define test-time compute in one sentence and name the two scaling axes it joined.
drills.a: Spending more inference-time compute per query (long internal reasoning chains) to buy accuracy — joining parameters+data (pretraining) and alignment/fine-tuning (post-training) as the third axis. Accuracy improves roughly logarithmically with thinking tokens.

drills.q: What reward signal does RL-on-chains use, and what behaviors emerge from it?
drills.a: Outcome rewards: the final answer is scored against a verifier (unit tests, exact-match, rubrics), and the policy is updated toward chains that produced correct answers. Emergent behaviors: longer chains on hard problems, backtracking ('wait, that's wrong'), re-derivation, approach-switching — reinforced because they correlate with success, not because scripted.

drills.q: Quote the AIME 2024 gap between non-reasoning and reasoning models, plus R1's number.
drills.a: GPT-4o-class ~13% vs o3-class ~96%; DeepSeek-R1 at 79.8% — an open-weight MIT-licensed model at roughly 5% of o1's API price. Also useful: GPQA-Diamond o3 87.7% / R1 71.5%.

drills.q: Why does a reasoning-model invoice look output-dominated when the visible answer is short?
drills.a: Hidden thinking tokens are billed as output: a typical query might be ~500 input tokens against ~5,000 output tokens of which ~4,500 are internal thinking. Hard problems scale to ~50k thinking tokens (~$0.40 o3-class) and hardest tiers to ~57M tokens/~14 min per question. Per-query cost becomes a distribution requiring budget tables and p95 alerting.

drills.q: Sketch the shape of the accuracy-vs-thinking-budget curve and its three corollaries.
drills.a: Logarithmic rise then plateau (sometimes degradation via overthinking loops). Corollaries: saturation points differ per task class (easy saturates in hundreds of tokens; unsolvable never rises); it composes with best-of-k/self-consistency at multiplicative cost; log-shape means budgets are marginal-return decisions, which is why APIs expose coarse effort tiers rather than raw token counts.

drills.q: Name four workload classes where a fast model beats a reasoner even at equal quality, with the mechanism.
drills.a: Chat (latency destroys UX); content generation (style bottleneck — indistinguishable outputs); simple lookups (nothing to compute); orchestration-bound agent loops (wall-clock dominated by tool calls/parsing so thinking premium is wasted); plus subjective/creative work. Mechanism in all: no accuracy gain to offset latency/cost penalties.

drills.q: Design the routing layer for a production assistant: what gets escalated and how do you handle runaway chains?
drills.a: Fast model default (~90% of traffic); escalate on low confidence (logprob/self-consistency signals), hard task classes, or explicit user request; reasoning-as-critic for drafts on critical paths. Runaway handling: token/time ceilings, n-gram repetition loop detectors, fallback to fast model with honest uncertainty signaling, per-task-class budget tables with p95 cost alerting since per-query cost is a distribution.

drills.q: Why can't you treat R1's visible <think> trace as an auditable causal record?
drills.a: Faithfulness gap: RL shapes chains statistically toward rewarded outcomes, so the displayed trace may rationalize a decision rather than reveal its actual causes. Visibility aids debugging and distillation but legibility ≠ faithfulness; compliance-critical flows need outcome-level verification and independent checks instead of chain-inspection certificates.

drills.q: A stakeholder says 'reasoning models solved hallucination.' Give the precise correction.
drills.a: They reduce manipulation-errors (multi-step arithmetic/logic where computation was the failure mode) but fabrication-tendency on missing knowledge persists — a reasoner constructs internally-consistent arguments from false premises fluently. What helps: retrieval grounding, citations, external verifiers, calibrated abstention, self-consistency. Diagnose your error regime before prescribing reasoning as medicine.

drills.q: Your agent spends 45s per action because every step calls a reasoner. Give the restructure plan and expected outcome.
drills.a: Profile steps into thinking-bound vs orchestration-bound; fast model executes routine steps; reserve reasoner for initial planning, critic-verification of consequential actions, and low-confidence recovery; add streaming status UX, parallel tool calls, cached context, per-step-type budget caps. Expected: reasoner touches ~10-20% of steps while task success holds — value comes from matching compute to step difficulty.

drills.q: R1's training recipe became public — does that make frontier reasoning cheap to produce? Distinguish carefully.
drills.a: No — it makes the RECIPE replicable and serving cheap (open weights, ~5% API pricing, distills). Training still consumed serious compute. The disruption was transparency and price pressure plus an open ecosystem; conflating serving cost with training cost is the classic error when citing R1 as 'reasoning is free now.'

drills.q: If inference efficiency improves 100x next year, does hybrid routing become obsolete? Argue both sides briefly.
drills.a: Obsolescence case: cheap-enough thinking removes the cost penalty from escalation. Counter-case: routing optimizes value-to-cost at the margin and cheap reasoning invites broader deployment where trivial-query waste multiplies too (Jevons dynamics); latency still matters regardless of price, and easy queries gain zero accuracy from any budget. Verdict: routing survives as policy even as thresholds move — build it configurable.
